paper.title: Transformer-generated atomic embeddings to enhance prediction accuracy of crystal properties with machine learning
paper.research_summary: This paper proposes a novel atomic embedding strategy called universal atomic embeddings (UAEs), generated by a custom-built CrystalTransformer model based on the Transformer architecture. The ct-UAEs are designed as broadly applicable atomic fingerprints that capture complex atomic features more effectively than traditional methods (e.g., one-hot encoding). Evaluated on formation energy and bandgap prediction across multiple databases (Materials Project, JARVIS, MC3D, hybrid perovskites), ct-UAEs consistently improve prediction accuracy—e.g., 14% MAE reduction for formation energy in CGCNN—and demonstrate strong transferability and interpretability via clustering and property correlation analysis.

tasks.objective: to generate universal atomic embeddings (UAEs) for broad applicability as atomic fingerprints that accurately capture complex atomic features and improve prediction accuracy of crystal properties
constraints: must be transferable across databases and tasks
must not rely on predeﬁned atomic attributes
must capture atomic roles and interactions within materials
input_requirements: atom input (one-hot encoding of atomic species)
output_goal: atomic embedding tensors (ct-UAEs) that serve as universal atomic fingerprints

evidence.text: Here, we proposed an atomic embedding strategy called universal atomic embeddings (UAEs) for their broad applicability as atomic ﬁngerprints, and generated the UAE tensors based on the proposed CrystalTransformer model.

stages.stage_name_raw: comparing atomic embeddings from different front-end models
stages.stage_goal: to evaluate and compare the performance of atomic embeddings generated by CrystalTransformer (Method I), GNN models (Method II), and artificially constructed features (Method III)
stage_input: atomic embeddings from Method II (GNN models)
atomic embeddings from Method III (artificially constructed)

evidence.text: As shown in Fig. 1a, for the front-end model, we used our proposed CrystalTransformer to generate atomic embeddings (Method I). Other pretrained atomic embeddings used GNN models (Method II shown in Fig. 1b). While some used artiﬁcially constructed features based on known atomic properties like the autoencoder-based approach43(Method III shown in Fig. 1c).

Table 1 shows a comparative MAE analysis to evaluate the relative performance enhancements attributable to the front-end atomic embeddings, denoted as N-CGCNN in Table 1 (N means the front-end model described above). As listed in Table 1, among the atomic embeddings pre-trained by different models, those who use ct-UAEs (CT-CGCNN) perform the best, with 14% and 7% reduction in MAE for Ef and Eg, also outperforming the best GNN front-end embeddings (CG-CGCNN in this context) by 4% and 5% for both properties, respectively.

stages.stage_name_raw: evaluating transferability of ct-UAEs across databases and tasks
stages.stage_goal: to test the ability and transferability of ct-UAEs on different databases (JARVIS, MC3D) and tasks (formation energy, bandgap, total energy, interatomic potential modeling)
stage_output: performance metrics for interatomic potential models

evidence.text: The ability and transferability of the universal atomic embedding are further tested on different databases and tasks. Each is cut into 8:1:1 for training, validation, and testing. Details on the dataset can be found in Supplementary 2A. As for the Jarvis dataset49, the result is shown in Table 1. The CT-CGCNN model demonstrates an improvement in predicting both formation energy Ef and bandgap energy Eg.
The embedding is further evaluated on the MC3D dataset. Properties such as total energy (E) are chosen as the task, and the result is shown in Table 1.
Additionally, we also investigated the suitability of ct-UAE on energy-conserving interatomic potential (IAP) models, which are trained based on the MPtrj dataset50.

stages.stage_name_raw: ablation study on coordinates part and multi-task variants
stages.stage_goal: to investigate the role of coordinates in CrystalTransformer and compare single-task vs. multi-task embeddings

evidence.text: To further investigate the role of the coordinates part of CrystalTransformer in model performance, an ablation study and qualitative analysis are conducted as described in Supplementary 7, which shows that the coordinates part encapsulates important geometric characteristics of crystal systems and is important in training the embeddings.

Further experiments focus on multi-task-generated embeddings (MT). As listed in Table 2, the embeddings trained from two properties (formation energy and bandgap), denoted as MT@2p, yield better performance compared to single-task-generated embeddings.

stages.stage_name_raw: clustering and interpretability analysis of ct-UAEs
stages.stage_goal: to project ct-UAEs into lower-dimensional space and cluster atoms to reveal connections between atomic features and targeted crystal properties
stage_output: violin plots of properties per class

evidence.text: This investigation leverages straightforward clustering algorithms to conduct an in-depth analysis of ct-UAEs. Here, the UMAP clustering method42 is employed to project these ct-UAEs into a two-dimensional space, thereby offering a means to intuitively understand atomic characteristics in a reduced dimensional setting.

Based on the clustering results, most of the elements in the periodic table can be categorized, as shown in Fig. 3a. This example divides all elements into 3 classes, called as Class A (the green cluster), Class B (the yellow cluster), and Class C (the blue cluster).
Front-end models as CrystalTransformer, CGCNN, ALIGNN, and MEGNET are ﬁrst pre-trained on the expanded MP* dataset, focusing on the bandgap energy Eg and formation energy Ef predictive tasks.
MP* denotes the 2023.6.23 version, which contains 134,243 materials.

To examine the atomic embeddings tensors obtained from different models, we used MP and MP* dataset for formation energy (Ef) and PBE bandgap (Eg), which are key properties for evaluating their chemical stabilities and electronic performances. MP stands for the 2018.6.1 version for MP44 dataset, which contains 69,239 materials with properties.
As for the Jarvis dataset49, the result is shown in Table 1. The CT-CGCNN model demonstrates an improvement in predicting both formation energy Ef and bandgap energy Eg.
The embedding is further evaluated on the MC3D dataset. Properties such as total energy (E) are chosen as the task, and the result is shown in Table 1.
Additionally, we also investigated the suitability of ct-UAE on energy-conserving interatomic potential (IAP) models, which are trained based on the MPtrj dataset50.

evidence.text: To further interpret the element classiﬁcation and without loss of generality, we chose oxide compounds from the Materials Project, which yielded a total of 62,068 retrieved materials. From these, we ﬁltered for those that contain data on formation energy, bandgap, and total magnetization.
